question.prompt: A telephone number has the form \(ABC-DEF-GHIJ,\) where each letter represents a different digit. The digits in each part of the number are in decreasing order; that is, \(A\gt B\gt C,\) \(D\gt E\gt F,\) and \(G\gt H\gt I\gt J.\) Furthermore, \(D,\) \(E,\) and \(F\) are consecutive even digits; \(G,\) \(H,\) \(I,\) and \(J\) are consecutive odd digits; and \(A+B+C=9.\) Find \(A.\)

solutions.explanation:
There are ten different letters and exactly ten available digits, so every digit from \(0\) through \(9\) occurs once. Their sum is \(45\). Since \(A+B+C=9\), the last two blocks have combined digit sum
\[
45-9=36.
\]
The decreasing triples of consecutive even digits can only be \(420\), \(642\), or \(864\), with digit sums \(6\), \(12\), and \(18\). The decreasing quadruples of consecutive odd digits can only be \(7531\) or \(9753\), with digit sums \(16\) and \(24\). These lists cover every possible block because the even digits are \(0,2,4,6,8\) and the odd digits are \(1,3,5,7,9\).

An odd-block sum of \(16\) would require an even-block sum of \(36-16=20\), which is unavailable. Thus the odd block is \(9753\), and the even block must have sum \(36-24=12\), making it \(642\).

The remaining digits are \(0,1,8\). In decreasing order they form \(810\), whose digits sum to \(9\). Hence \(A=8\), choice E.
solutions.title: Use the sum of all ten digits
